initial_reasons.WILL: Enters cautiously, trying to read Agnes's response to the new house.
initial_reasons.AGNES: Remains fixed on Will with grief and resentment already close beneath the surface.

WILL.reason: Hearing Hamnet's death named in this house brings guilt forward and briefly breaks his eye contact.
His admission that he is constantly wondering begins an active mental search for Hamnet.
The repeated question of where Hamnet is exposes the frightening intensity of his fixation.
His apology is a direct attempt to acknowledge the harm his absence has caused.
Agnes's description of a place in his head forces him to confront how she sees his withdrawal.
Hearing that even Hamnet's death could not draw him back turns his guilt into visible shame.
The accusation that he should have been present confronts him with the farewell he lost.

AGNES.reason: The question of why Will withheld the house tour immediately exposes her suspicion of his motives.
Hearing that Will is still searching reveals that his grief, though distant, has not ended.
Will's measure of a year provokes her insistence that grief has been continuous from the moment of death.
Hearing the apology without an explanation makes her challenge what Will is actually sorry for.
She asserts that Will's inner world has become more real to him than their shared life.
Naming Hamnet's death strips away the argument and reveals the wound beneath her anger.
She presses the final charge that Will was denied, and denied Hamnet, a last farewell.
